- Overestimate prices after recent spikes; model tends to overshoot post-peak sentiment (e.g., +0.70 sentiment → forecast peaks then drops too slowly).
- Underestimate when sentiment turns sharply positive (e.g., +0.70 → model fails to adjust downward quickly).
- Lag in correction: model often delays mean reversion after strong negative sentiment (e.g., -0.70 → forecast stays high for 2–3 days).
- Bias toward high values when sentiment is neutral or mildly negative (e.g., -0.30 → model still forecasts 45+ despite recent dip).
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts overreact to short-term sentiment shifts; 10-day forecasts better capture sentiment-driven corrections.
- Avoid extrapolating recent trend if sentiment reverses; model often ignores sentiment reversal in 3–5 day window.
